first_impression.reaction: I googled 'mauritius wedding' because it's on our shortlist next to Italy, and the first thing my dad will ask is whether it's 'properly legal'. The intro answers that straight away: send the documents to Port Louis, have the originals checked in person, 24-hour publication, Civil Status Officer. No 'say I do in paradise', which is a relief. I read the documents and Port Louis sections properly and would send them to James, skimmed the weather and travel-advice bits. It is very good on paperwork, but it barely mentions our guests and doesn't tell me anything about which part of the island to pick.

journey.quote: Mauritius is on the shortlist, and before you fall for a lagoon you want to know one thing: will the marriage count? It will.
journey.reaction: That's exactly where we are. A straight answer first, then the steps behind it. As a lawyer I like that it names the process rather than promising it's easy.

journey.section: Can Australians marry legally in Mauritius?
journey.quote: Read it once, together, before you sign anything with a resort.
journey.reaction: Pointing us at the government page instead of hiding it behind an enquiry form is a trust signal. It doesn't feel like they're trying to keep the information to themselves.

journey.quote: Some couples keep the civil marriage small and early in the day, with only their witnesses, then gather everyone on the sand at dusk for the vows they have written.
journey.reaction: This is the personal, not-a-resort-package version we'd actually want. Helpful to see it laid out as an option.

journey.section: What the Civil Status Division asks for
journey.quote: The 3-month window is the detail that catches couples out.
journey.reaction: The kind of thing only someone who has watched it go wrong would say. I'd have ordered the birth certificates the week we booked. Sending this bit to James.

journey.section: If you are asked to show you are not already married
journey.quote: Some countries ask for proof that you are not already married.
journey.reaction: So does Mauritius ask for it or not? The list above doesn't include a CNI, then this section talks about 'some countries'. I read it twice and still don't know whether we need to order one.

journey.quote: Put this visit at the start of the trip, before the welcome drinks and the spa days.
journey.reaction: Clear action tied to our itinerary. But I still don't know how many days that actually is. Every answer ends with 'ask the Civil Status Office', so I can't book flights from this page alone.

journey.section: Who performs the ceremony, and where
journey.quote: A fee applies for a wedding in a hotel or other premises, and it is paid at the Central Civil Status Office.
journey.reaction: How much? It's the one government cost in the whole process and there's no number or even a range. Probably small, but it's the hidden-cost thing we worry about.

journey.section: Who performs the ceremony, and where
journey.quote: Treat the Officer's transport as part of the run sheet, with a car, a driver and a named person who meets them at the gate.
journey.reaction: Love this. A named person at the gate is exactly the 'someone accountable on the day' we want. Insider detail.

journey.quote: Ask the Office, too, whether the Officer will ask you to choose a matrimonial regime (the legal arrangement for property within the marriage) and which options apply to two non-citizens.
journey.reaction: As a lawyer this one makes me sit up. It's flagged but not explained, which leaves me slightly worried. Is this a real thing we have to decide on the day? A sentence on what the default is would help.

journey.section: Getting your certificate ready for Australia
journey.quote: You cannot register an overseas marriage in Australia.
journey.reaction: Clear. Then the subheading 'Recognition and registering at home' a few paragraphs later made me think I'd missed a step, because it's actually about not marrying twice and a lunch at home.

journey.section: Ceremonies on the beach or at your resort
journey.reaction: The question list for the resort is genuinely useful and I'd copy it into our notes. Honest that the venue holds the answers, not the article.

journey.quote: Mean temperature: 24.7 degrees Celsius in summer and 20.4 degrees Celsius in winter.
journey.reaction: Skimmed. The cyclone and spare-day point is the useful bit. The averages read like an encyclopaedia and don't tell me which month is best for 80 guests.

journey.quote: Where you marry on the island changes the light you marry in.
journey.reaction: Great opening line, then it never names a single coast. No north, east, west or south, no 'suits a couple who...'. I came out of this section knowing coasts get more sun than the plateau and nothing else. This is the decision we actually face.

journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans your venue, travel, vendors and payments as one point of contact from start to finish, and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: One contact and inclusions in writing is what we want. But 'start to finish' is the end-to-end line every planner uses, and there's no Mauritius venue or wedding here to back it.

journey.section: Plan your Mauritius wedding with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, quotes in AUD, and agrees the fee in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: AUD and fee in writing directly hit the currency-surprise fear. Calm close, no hard sell. Not enough on its own to make me enquire.

What do our international guests need for entry, and which months are easiest for older relatives flying from Australia?
Who is actually on the ground in Mauritius on the day: your own person or a local partner? (deferred business detail)
Do you have a real Mauritius wedding (venue, coast, date) we can look at? (deferred business detail)
How does Wedded Wonderland charge: flat fee, percentage, commissions? Is there a starting range? (deferred business detail)
Will you help with the document pack, the Port Louis appointment and the Apostille, or is that on us? (deferred business detail)
Do you arrange airport transfers for guests, and the Officer's transport? (deferred business detail)
Are there perks or Wedded Privileges at Mauritius resorts? (deferred business detail)
How many Mauritius weddings have you planned? (deferred business detail)

turn_offs_found.quote: A fee applies for a wedding in a hotel or other premises, and it is paid at the Central Civil Status Office.
turn_offs_found.why: The only cost in the legal process is left without a figure or range. Vague pricing makes me wonder what else isn't spelled out.

turn_offs_found.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans your venue, travel, vendors and payments as one point of contact from start to finish
turn_offs_found.why: 'Start to finish' is the generic end-to-end claim every planner makes. Without a Mauritius wedding or a named person on the ground, it sits flatter than the very specific advice above it.

would_share_with: James: the 'What the Civil Status Division asks for' and 'In Port Louis' sections, because the 3-month birth certificate window and the arrival visit decide when we both fly
My parents: the intro and the 'Is a civil marriage in Mauritius recognised in Australia?' FAQ, because Dad will ask whether it's legal at home

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [start a conversation with Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=mauritius-wedding&utm_content=closing).
cta_reaction.why: No pressure, and AUD plus fee in writing are the right reassurances. But we're 14 months out, Mauritius is one of a few options, and I haven't seen a real Mauritius wedding from them. I'd read the African destinations page first and come back.

top_3_changes: Make 'Choosing your coast' actually name the coasts and say who each suits (light, wind, distance to the airport and Port Louis, ease for older guests), because 'Where you marry on the island changes the light you marry in.' sets up a comparison the section never delivers.

Clear up the CNI question: say plainly whether the Division's list for two non-citizens includes one, since 'Some countries ask for proof that you are not already married.' leaves us unsure whether to order one.

Add one or two lines for guests (entry, cyclone-season spare day, transfers from the airport) and fix the 'Recognition and registering at home' heading, since the page has just said you cannot register the marriage.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection

No invented brand facts; fees, commissions, on-the-ground team, real weddings, scale, perks, Privileges, transfers and paperwork help listed as deferred unanswered questions, not must-fix
VERIFY markers and HTML comments (fact tags, image slots) ignored

open_questions.question: Does the source pack say whether a CNI is required for two non-citizens in Mauritius? If not, can the CNI section say so explicitly?
Is the Civil Status Office fee for hotel or premises ceremonies published, so a figure or range can replace 'A fee applies'?
Is there sourced material to name the coasts and their character, so 'Choosing your coast' can compare them?

assumptions: Sophie & James arrived via a Google search for 'mauritius wedding' with Mauritius on a shortlist, so relevance is 4 and enquiry likelihood is 2 (they enquire after 2 to 3 posts plus a real wedding).

Business details (Wedded Wonderland fees and amounts, commissions, on-the-ground team, real weddings, scale proof, perks, Privileges, transfers, paperwork help) are deliberately deferred and not penalised as must-fix.

The 3-minute budget covered the intro, key takeaways, legal, documents, Port Louis, ceremony, certificate, beach, coast sections and the close in full, with a skim of travel advice, climate and the FAQ.
